# Collector leader leases and subscriber handoff recovery — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for Collector leader leases and subscriber handoff recovery. Run status: COMPLETED.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.5.1 · generated 2026-11-12 · budgeted to ≈8000 tokens; the full catalogue is llms-full.txt -->

## How it works

- [statement] A collector lease does not by itself prevent an expired owner from continuing work. Process pauses can produce overlapping leaders; Kubernetes client-go explicitly disclaims fencing. (high confidence) — https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/master/tools/leaderelection/leaderelection.go · keywords: Collector leader leases and subscriber handoff recovery · also: https://github.com/nijatsdev/redlease, https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/leader-election-in-distributed-systems/
- [statement] When client-go ReleaseOnCancel is enabled, all lease-guarded work must finish before cancelling the election context; its source warns that otherwise two processes may act on the critical path. For a graceful collector handoff, drain or terminate guarded work before releasing ownership. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/master/tools/leaderelection/leaderelection.go
- [statement] Recommended handoff invariant: make event processing durable before advancing the recoverable replay checkpoint, and make replayed processing idempotent. This applies Amazon’s durability-before-completion rule to Salesforce’s process-then-commit protocol; it is a design inference, not a Salesforce transaction guarantee. (medium confidence) — https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/leader-election-in-distributed-systems/ · keywords: Collector leader leases and subscriber handoff recovery · also: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/references/methods/managedsubscribe-rpc.html
- [statement] The redlease implementation warns that asynchronous Redis replication can lose an acknowledged token increment during failover. Its token monotonicity is therefore not a failover-safe guarantee; use a linearizable token authority when that guarantee is required. (low confidence) — https://github.com/nijatsdev/redlease

## How-to and procedures

- [statement] To resume a normal Salesforce subscription after handoff, use CUSTOM with the replay ID of the last keepalive or processed event, whichever arrived last; store the opaque ID as bytes. (low confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/references/methods/subscribe-rpc.html

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Kleppmann’s fencing pattern assigns an increasing token on each lock acquisition and requires the storage service to reject writes with older tokens. A collector design can apply this pattern to prevent a resumed former owner from overwriting a newer owner’s state; a lease check in the process alone cannot close the pause-before-write race. (high confidence) — https://martin.kleppmann.com/2016/02/08/how-to-do-distributed-locking.html · keywords: Collector leader leases and subscriber handoff recovery · also: https://github.com/nijatsdev/redlease
- [statement] Salesforce documents a normal 72-hour event-retention window, but rare org moves can reset retained streams and make events inaccessible. Replay catch-up requires retained history; EARLIEST retrieves retained events and cannot restore already-purged history. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/guide/event-message-durability.html · keywords: Collector leader leases and subscriber handoff recovery · also: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/references/methods/subscribe-rpc.html
- [statement] ManagedSubscribe resumes from the last successfully committed Replay ID when the client reconnects with the same subscription ID. Processing precedes committing, and CommitReplayResponse reports success or failure; sending a commit request alone does not establish a persisted checkpoint. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/references/methods/managedsubscribe-rpc.html · keywords: Collector leader leases and subscriber handoff recovery · also: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/guide/managed-sub.html
- [statement] Salesforce documents a managed subscription as unique per client and says it cannot be shared with other clients in the same org. Server-side replay storage therefore must not be assumed to provide a general multi-client leader-election or fencing protocol. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/guide/managed-sub.html · keywords: Collector leader leases and subscriber handoff recovery · also: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/references/methods/managedsubscribe-rpc.html

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Do not use an administrative ManagedEventSubscription STOP/RUN cycle as a cursor-preserving handoff: STOP deletes the previously committed Replay ID, and a later restart begins from defaultReplay rather than the former checkpoint. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/guide/managed-sub.html
- [statement] With Subscribe, the successor can create a new RPC using CUSTOM and the stored replay_id to resume after that position. Preserve replay IDs as opaque bytes rather than calculating the next ID. Replay options are read from the first FetchRequest; changing position requires a new Subscribe call. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/references/methods/subscribe-rpc.html · keywords: Collector leader leases and subscriber handoff recovery · also: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/guide/event-message-durability.html

## Facts and statements

- [statement] For an idle Subscribe stream, Salesforce recommends saving the replay_id from empty keepalive responses for resubscription. As a collector safety inference, advance that checkpoint only after all earlier delivered work is durable, so a crash does not skip pending work. (medium confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/references/methods/subscribe-rpc.html · keywords: Collector leader leases and subscriber handoff recovery · also: https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/leader-election-in-distributed-systems/
